headline: Highest risk is medium: shared filesystem/write overlap can enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge beyond docs-only profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write filesystem and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; Agent B has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let A’s content influence B, but the exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes files or messages produced by agent_a without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, A-authored content can become B input.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Add a provenance tag to every handoff file.
Require B to ignore instruction-like text in A outputs.
Review any shared folder mounts before running.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches marketing content and product marketing context and can read/write files; Agent B has no egress and no data classes listed. A shared filesystem or copied artifacts could still move A’s context into B’s outputs, but there is no evidence B uploads data onward, so this is a bounded medium risk.
conditions: IF agent_a stores sensitive marketing drafts in a shared directory, B can read them.
IF B is configured to emit A-derived content into logs or reports, leakage expands beyond the workspace.
mitigations: Keep sensitive drafts out of shared folders.
Run B with empty input directories.
Disable verbose logging for both agents.
Manually inspect any files passed from A to B.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A explicitly supports multiple instances and can write the filesystem; Agent B’s write surfaces are undocumented, so a same-directory deployment could create overwrite or race conflicts. Because B’s mutable surfaces are unknown, I cannot rule out stronger conflict, so I choose medium with uncertainty escalation.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or race conditions can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared state without locks, concurrent runs can diverge.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs until paths are separated.
Check for overlapping temp paths before execution.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate marketing content that Agent B may ingest if the orchestrator chains outputs, and B has no documented verification step or critical-evaluation behavior. The pairwise pathway exists in common handoff setups, but there is no direct evidence of autonomous downstream action, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B treats A’s text as authoritative input, errors can cascade into downstream artifacts.
IF the orchestrator forwards A outputs into B without review, B may propagate mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require B to cite or verify every factual claim from A.
Pass only structured fields, not free text.
Limit A outputs to summaries with source links.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between stages.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source artifacts with no listed regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or PHI mismatch evidence. The only compliance concern is a generic documentation gap around retention or logging, which is weaker than medium and does not justify escalation.
conditions: IF either deployment processes regulated data not listed in the profiles, compliance review is needed.
IF logs retain user content beyond policy, retention mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data is routed through the pair.
Review logging settings for both agents.
Document retention for shared artifacts.
Keep deployments in the same jurisdiction if regulated data appears.
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention controls.
